exposure: gestational age at birth (22-24 weeks vs. 25-28 weeks)
fetal growth (appropriate-for-gestational age [AGA] vs. small-for-gestational age [SGA])
cohort: The study included 81 infants born at <=28 weeks of gestation between 2018 and 2022 at a single hospital.
finding: Persistent renal insufficiency, specifically significantly higher urine albumin levels, was observed around term equivalent age in peri-viable infants, especially in appropriate-for-gestational age infants born at 22-24 weeks compared to those born at 25-28 weeks.
gest_age: <=28 weeks of gestation (specifically 22-24 weeks and 25-28 weeks)
